services.story: The same home visit when Alex's health plan pays in network, with a doctor's referral. Nothing is taken, and Lee Home Nutrition bills the plan its own way.

services_shape: one client with one dietitian at a time, each visit a set length: a 60-minute first nutrition visit (the assessment), then 30-minute follow-ups agreed at the visit and OK'd by the client by text; a new client may ask for a free 15-minute intro call first; a parent or guardian comes with anyone under 18
questions_before_times: for you (18 or older), or for your child or teen (a parent or guardian books and comes)
which state you'll be in during the visit (a dietitian must be licensed there, by video too)
a health plan (its name only), or paying yourself
has a doctor sent a referral: yes, not yet, or no
at the clinic, by video, or at your home (the town, for a home visit or a store tour)
safety_stop: a medical emergency: fainting, confusion, chest pain, trouble breathing, or very high or very low blood sugar the person can't bring back
signs of an eating disorder: making yourself throw up, using laxatives to get rid of food, going days without eating, or a strong fear of gaining weight
license: always for medical nutrition therapy: a dietitian's own license where the state's form licenses dietitians, or the national dietitian registration (RDN) as the proof where the state's form has no license (a switch)
staff_skills: who sees adults, teens and families; who offers video, home visits and grocery store tours; who speaks which language; who is trained for eating-disorder care (booked only by the clinic's team, by phone); a dietitian with a provisional license works under a supervisor
messages_never: client texts carry only the business name, the date, the time, the place and a secure link: never the kind of visit, a condition, a weight, lab results, a medicine name, food or eating details, or a child's details; at home and at a store, the dietitian's name and photo stay, for the door check; the video link stays on the secure page
